title: Manchester City Sign Elliot Anderson for Record €135 Million From Nottingham Forest
excerpt: The 23-year-old England international becomes the most expensive signing in Manchester City's history and the costliest English player ever, marking the first major acquisition of the Enzo Maresca era.
body:
• Manchester City have signed midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for €135 million, a club-record fee and the most ever paid for an English player.
  • Anderson, 23, signed a five-year contract and completed his medical in Kansas while on World Cup duty with England.
  • The deal marks the first major signing under new manager Enzo Maresca, who succeeded Pep Guardiola at the end of last season.

City Shatter Transfer Records

https://youtube.com/watch?v=pFMo2zjt1eI

Manchester City have completed the signing of England midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for a reported €135 million (£116 million), the club confirmed on July 2. The fee eclipses the £100 million City paid for Jack Grealish in 2021 and ranks among the top five most expensive transfers in football history.

https://x.com/FutbolHub_/status/2080326296307929530

Performance-related bonuses could push the total package to as much as €150 million, according to English media reports, which would also set a new British transfer record. The deal surpasses the £105 million Arsenal spent on Declan Rice and Alexander Isak's £125 million move to Liverpool.

Anderson, 23, has signed a five-year contract. His medical was conducted in Kansas City, where the England squad was based during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

"City are one of the biggest clubs in the world and the squad they have is amazing — so strong in every position. As soon as I knew they wanted me, I was absolutely determined to make this move happen."

— Elliot Anderson

A Remarkable Rise

Anderson's trajectory has been steep. He joined Nottingham Forest from Newcastle United just two years ago for €42 million — a sale Newcastle made to comply with the Premier League's Profit and Sustainability Rules. Former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe later described that departure as "the most painful sale of my coaching career."

At Forest, Anderson developed into one of the Premier League's most complete midfielders. Last season, he made 50 appearances across all competitions, contributing four goals and five assists. He topped the Premier League in total touches (3,300), ball recoveries (306), successful tackles (297), and fouls won (80) — statistical dominance that attracted serious interest from multiple top clubs.

Forest rejected City's first two bids before accepting the third proposal. Personal terms had already been agreed.

The Maresca Era Begins

Anderson is the first major signing since Pep Guardiola stepped down at the end of last season, ushering in the Enzo Maresca era at the Etihad Stadium. The former Chelsea boss inherits a squad in transition, with Kevin De Bruyne's departure leaving a significant void in midfield creativity.

City director of football Hugo Viana framed the signing as a long-term investment in the club's midfield architecture.

"Elliot is one of the outstanding young midfield talents in world football right now. He offers energy, outstanding work rate and an exceptional range of passing. At just 23, there is plenty of opportunity for development over the coming years and we feel he can become a complete midfielder."

— Hugo Viana, Manchester City Director of Football

Anderson joins a midfield that already includes Tijjani Reijnders, whom City signed from AC Milan last summer for €70 million, and the returning Rodri. The trio gives Maresca a potent combination of industry, technical quality, and tactical versatility as he looks to reassert City's domestic dominance after a relatively underwhelming title defence.

What's Next

Anderson was a key member of Thomas Tuchel's England squad at the 2026 World Cup, where the team won bronze. He is expected to arrive in Manchester after a post-tournament break and begin integrating with the squad ahead of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

For Nottingham Forest, the record fee provides significant reinvestment firepower. Lucas Bergvall of Tottenham Hotspur and Davide Frattesi of Inter Milan have been identified as leading candidates to fill the Anderson-shaped hole in Forest's midfield.

City's spending under the Maresca rebuild is now well underway. Whether the investment translates into a return to the summit of English football will be the defining question of the season ahead.
